#### 1. Moyamoya disease 5  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.780)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:130)

**Proposed mechanism:** ACTA2 (HGNC:130) —DISRUPTS→ Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036); Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebral small vessel disease (HP:0033112); Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036) —LEADS_TO→ Intracranial arterial calcification (HP:0034001). Haploinsufficiency of ACTA2 disrupts actin cytoskeleton organization, leading to cerebral small vessel disease (characteristic of Moyamoya disease 5) and intracranial arterial calcification (a phenotype observed in related disorders potentially linked to ACTA2 dysfunction).

**How to falsify it:** Absence of ACTA2 mutations in patients diagnosed with both conditions, or identification of distinct causal genes with no overlap in functional pathways. _(variant: Exome Variant Frequency > 0.01 for ACTA2 variants in relevant populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting pathways involved in actin dynamics and vascular integrity could offer therapeutic strategies for both conditions.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of actin isoforms in these distinct but mechanistically related thrombocytopenias could inform therapeutic strategies.
